doc: QR of a 3x3 matrix g drawn from the normal distribution (g is the INPUT: the draw), then the columns of q are multiplied by sign(diag(r)) (which makes the factorization unique, so any QR algorithm gives this q), then column 0 is negated when det(q) < 0, so the result is a proper rotation (det +1). 34 matrices: the identity, -I, diag(1,1,-1) (the determinant flip), permutation and triangular ones with negative diagonals, 24 random normal matrices, and two scaled by 1e3 and 1e-3 (the rotation is scale free). The flip of column 0 is taken for 20 of the 34 and not for the others (checked at build time; condition numbers below 1e3). The Python function takes a numpy Generator and calls rng.normal(size=(3, 3)) once: the case replaces that draw by the input g (a port's equivalent is a function of g, params.rng_draw). float64 closed form: rtol 1e-9, atol 1e-12.

params.rng_draw: g = rng.normal(size=(3, 3)), float64, the only draw _random_rotation makes
params.stand_in: q = _random_rotation(rng) where rng.normal(size=(3, 3)) returns the input g
